text:
Maya (support): We have a live customer (acct: acme-ml) reporting a spike of 5xx errors on inference calls since ~09:10 UTC. Customer says sudden failure rate ~25% and latency >10s for some requests. They pasted a few error snippets and curl repro.

Liam (eng-sre): Can you drop the raw curl and the exact error bodies/log IDs? Also which model + region?

Maya (support): Pasted from customer: `curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME' -d '{"model":"gpt-neo-rlm","input":"hello"}'` => response: `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway` and body `{ "error": "upstream error: service returned 500" }`. They also included request IDs: RQ: rq_0a7f2c, rq_0a7f9e, rq_0a7fa3. Region: us-west-2, model pinned to gpt-neo-rlm@v3.

Aria (eng-runtime): Thanks. I just looked at our gateway traces for us-west-2 around those RQ ids. The gateway returned a 502/504 after timing out waiting on quota-orchestrator (internal service) which returned 500 on several RPCs. I see repeated "rpc error: context deadline exceeded" from quota-orchestrator to redis and also a few TCP resets.

Liam (eng-sre): Ok that suggests a misroute or a slow dependency in quota-orchestrator. Could be that quota-orchestrator v1 is hitting a bad redis shard and returning 500 instead of instructing gateway to return 4xx when quota exceeded. That would explain 5xx propagation.

Maya (support): The customer insists they did not change anything client-side. Their dashboard shows a lot of 5xx starting 09:10 -> 09:45 and then sporadic.

ops-bot: Incident alert: quota-orchestrator error rate > 5% in us-west-2 (service=quota-orchestrator, error_type=500, window=5m). Pager duty: on-call notified.

Liam (eng-sre): I'm pulling logs from quota-orchestrator. Snippet: ```
2026-02-14T09:12:31.124Z ERROR orchestrator/handler.go:87 handleQuotaRequest failed: rpc error: code=13 desc="connection error: deadline exceeded"
2026-02-14T09:12:31.125Z WARN orchestrator/cache.go:210 redis: read tcp 10.2.3.11:6379: i/o timeout
2026-02-14T09:12:31.126Z ERROR orchestrator/api.go:143 respondWithError status=500 msg="dependency timeout"
```

Aria (eng-runtime): I also see gateway traces where the gateway calls quota-orchestrator and gets back 5xx, then gateway does not map it to 429 (which we expect for quota hits). The route policy for quota-service has a fallback set to 'propagate' which causes gateway to propagate 5xx instead of transforming dependency-timeout into 4xx. Looks like a config change in routing from last week.

Liam (eng-sre): Repro steps I ran locally: repeated curl with a small token and short timeout https://internal-gateway.svc/quota-check -> when orchestrator hits redis timeout it returns 500. Example: ```
$ curl -v -H "X-Request-ID: rq-debug" http://internal:10003/check?key=acme
< HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
{"error":"dependency timeout"}
```

Jin (product): Is this actually a quota limit (should be 4xx) or a dependency outage? Customer impact is different. If orchestrator can't reach redis it should surface a transient 5xx but gateway should treat quota-check failures as "failed to validate" and either fallback to permissive or return 4xx? We need to check product intent.

Aria (eng-runtime): Product intent: quota-check RPC should return: 200 (allowed), 429 (quota exceeded), or 4xx for malformed requests. Dependency timeouts should be treated as 503/timeout upstream but gateway must not return raw 500 when customer request is valid. Historically we had a mapping where orchestrator-level dependency timeouts were mapped to a gateway-check-result of "indeterminate" that triggered a 4xx with code 'quota_check_indeterminate' (client visible 429-ish semantics). That mapping seems to be undone in the policy change pushed on 2026-02-08.

Liam (eng-sre): For short-term mitigation I'm going to flip gateway routing to prefer the secondary orchestrator (v2) which has improved redis timeouts and a defensive 4xx mapping. Applying now.

Maya (support): Please confirm and I'll let the customer know we have a mitigation.

Liam (eng-sre): Patch applied: `kubectl patch svc gateway --patch '{"spec":{"trafficPolicy":{"quotaServicePrecedence":"v2,primary"}}}'` -> Confirmed traffic shifted to quota-orchestrator-v2 pods. Error rate dropped to ~0.5% within 60s.

ops-bot: Deploy event: routing patch applied by liam. Deployment: gateway-config-20260214-1649.

Maya (support): Customer confirmed that errors dropped to near 0 and latencies back to normal. They asked what caused this and if they need to do anything.

Aria (eng-runtime): Root cause appears to be two-fold: 1) Redis shard us-west-2-a had transient I/O timeouts (cloud provider network flaps) causing quota-orchestrator v1 to start returning 500; 2) a config rollout last week removed the previous defensive mapping in gateway policy so dependency timeouts from orchestrator propagated as 5xx to customers instead of being translated to client-visible quota semantics.

Liam (eng-sre): Immediate follow-ups: - revert the policy change to enforce mapping for dependency timeouts -> 4xx semantics. - add circuit-breaker on gateway calling quota-orchestrator to fail fast and return controlled 4xx. - increase redis client timeouts and add multi-shard retries in orchestrator.

Jin (product): Longer term: we should decide expected semantics when quota service can't be reached. Triage doc should include explicit mapping rules. I'll create a short RFC for the team to approve. Also need to decide whether we want gateway to be permissive (allow) or conservative (deny) on indeterminate checks.

Liam (eng-sre): I'll open follow-up tickets and link them here. Quick tickets: IR-3491 revert-gateway-timeout-mapping, IR-3492 orchestrator-redis-retries, IR-3493 add-circuit-breaker-gateway->quota.

Aria (eng-runtime): Also adding observability: a dedicated metric for "quota-orchestrator.dependency_timeouts_count" and an alert that triggers earlier (currently thresholds were too high).

Maya (support): I'll close the customer loop and send a summary: root cause, mitigation, timeline, and planned follow-ups.

Liam (eng-sre): Postmortem owners: Liam + Aria. ETA for full writeup: EOD tomorrow.

Jin (product): Flagging for compliance: if any customers in regulated sectors were affected we need extra notification; list is in compliance-runbook.

Maya (support): Thanks team. Customer happy with mitigation and will reach out if they see recurrence.

Liam (eng-sre): Final note: we saw ~3% of requests in that window returned 502/504 from the gateway due to propagated 500s. Remediation summary: route -> v2, patch policy back, schedule infra fixes.

ops-bot: Incident resolved: quota-orchestrator incident in us-west-2 mitigated.
